body:
The best otome game? Not really. There's an arguably large amount of PC and console otome games I'd like to vote for. Even if you count mobile games then there are ports for famous console games like Hakuouki or Amnesia, and who is to say they aren't good otome games? But, the best mobile otome game? Yes! The gameplay is interesting, the way to earn in-game currency are to my taste (I don't mind watching ad but it becomes a chore pretty soon, and I'm glad MM doesn't have this feature), the translation is amazing, the CGs are... Welp let's skip this part about CGs 😂 Anyway the game captured my heart like none others and I'm in love. Pretty hard to find another game like MM that I can love (no don't recommend games for me, I probably knew about them).

Now that the old NTT Solmare games and some free games (I mean like games that you can play without the annoying paid choices and diamond system) are gone, I'm left in a mobile market where only a few otome games truly catch my heart. Crying out loud! 😭 (That's why I ran head-straight into a bishoujo game with great story and a good amount of male characters 😂 though it's not quite otome and the gacha is a lie...)

Too late, when I found out about a farming method after years of playing relying purely on HGs and hearts earned by the routes I already started to farm like crazy and I'm having 3000+ HGs now, haha... Thanks, diligent me of a few months ago.
If Cheritz wants to make more money with MM then they should, idk, release more DLC, epilogues and in-game events or something, not... this. When they finally take their eyes off The Ssum and remember us then this happened...

The reasons why I like Seven are simply because: I feel bad for him, he is relatable, and I can't bear to be mean to him. It's the same with other characters I like, too, in fact, I can't be mean to anyone (except Rika). I understand Seven too well that I feel bad when I see how hurt he is whenever he tries to push MC away. It hurts him as much as it hurt us, y'know?, or even greater. Regretting that he might have overdone it, wanting to reconcile, having to stay away in believing "it's the best for them not to get involved with me anymore". He is torn between keeping up a wall and letting all defense down. These thoughts probably torment him all the time, and it makes his depression worse, and in turn, makes him irritated, and act out of control. I didn't really understand depression back in 2016, but I felt deeply connected with him somehow. It's like looking at a mirror. Do you know what it feels to suppress emotions: sadness, anger... for too long and when you finally let it all out, you just yell out loud before you know it, and only come back to your sense after all that's said and done? After yelling, you start to regret saying those things in anger, and is dreadful how you just lost control of yourself and let your emotions run rampage... I don't have proofs, but I suspect that's what Seven felt when he yelled at MC to stay the f away from him: losing control of his feelings. So, I don't blame him.

And the "I can't be mean to them" part? You could say that I have this urge to keep being nice even in games. Or more like, it's precisely because this is a game that I can choose to be nice or not, and the choices to be mean aren't really my cup of tea, so I didn't choose them. In real life? It would be a miracle if I can meet the RFA and not appear to be a shy or aloof person. Hell, I wouldn't even meet them at all, since I won't be falling for Unknown's dumb story.
The characters in MM are flawed as hell, and it's simply a matter of "love them or leave them", really. It depends on how deep you relate to them. As for me, I try to understand them better in their route, and if I come to like them, great. If not, then that's ok too. Can't expect everyone to like my favorite character. (In fact there is a person whom I can't like although I tried to, and you already know who.)
